'''George Paxton Young''' (9 November 1818 – 26 February 1889) was a Canadian philosopher and professor of logic, metaphysics and ethics at the [[University of Toronto]].<ref>{{cite web |title=George Paxton Young |url=https://www.thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/george-paxton-young |website=The Canadian Encyclopedia}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Biography – YOUNG, GEORGE PAXTON – Volume XI (1881-1890) – Dictionary of Canadian Biography |url=http://www.biographi.ca/en/bio/young_george_paxton_11E.html |website=www.biographi.ca}}</ref> He studied the quintic polynomial equation and in 1888 described how to solve a solvable quintic equation, without providing an explicit formula.<ref>George Paxton Young, "Solvable Quintic Equations with Commensurable Coefficients", ''American Journal of Mathematics'' '''10''':99–130 (1888), {{JSTOR|2369502}}</ref>

==George Paxton Young Memorial Prize==
The Department of Philosophy at the University of Toronto grants the George Paxton Young Memorial Prize annually to students who read a refereed philosophy paper at an international, national or regional philosophy conference.<ref>{{cite web |title=Honours and Awards |url=https://philosophy.utoronto.ca/st-george/graduate/honours-and-awards/ |website=Department of Philosophy}}</ref>
